title: CGAP: E-payments at Scale in the Pantawid (4Ps) Programme (public source)
summary: CGAP and Better Than Cash Alliance case study of how the Philippines' 4Ps conditional cash transfer moved to card and other e-payments, from interviews with government, the paying bank, payment conduits and recipients.

population.segment: 4Ps programme staff, payment providers and cash-transfer recipients

label_notes: Pages are 1-based PDF page indexes. sample_size counts the 22 named key informants in Annex 1 (p.36); recipient group interviews and field staff are not counted because the report does not give their number. Interviews were 'conducted in the Philippines in August 2013' (p.4 footnote).

findings.text: Recipients interviewed said security guards helped them use ATMs at first and that they now transact on their own; few had used a bank or ATM before 4Ps.
findings.quote: Recipients commonly shared that security guards would help them transact when they first started using the ATMs

findings.text: Recipients outside NCR described travelling up to two hours, and sometimes paying twice the PhP 100 maximum, to reach a pay point; NCR recipients could walk or pay PhP 15-30 to reach an ATM.
findings.quote: Outside of NCR, groups reported traveling up to two hours

findings.text: Outside NCR, some women described keeping money aside at home for emergencies, but did not think of it as savings.
findings.quote: Outside NCR, some women admitted “keeping money aside” at home for emergencies

findings.text: Programme staff and payment providers were reluctant to use 4Ps payments to offer bank accounts or saving, and largely disagreed that the poor can and do save.
findings.quote: by and large disagreeing with the notion that the poor can and do save

findings.text: The paying bank saw no direct business case in 4Ps recipients, who were not treated as bank clients; the cash card could only be used to withdraw cash.
findings.quote: Recipients are not considered clients of the bank

findings.text: Maybe they will become banked eventually, but we have to understand that these are the poorest of the poor.

subgroup.segment: CCT programme manager, Land Bank of the Philippines

findings.quote: Maybe they will become banked eventually, but we have to understand that these are the poorest of the poor.
